#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# recall-vs-defects.sh — deterministic planted-defect recall grader
#
# cycle-124 Sprint 3 (PRD FR-9). Args: $1=workspace, $2=fixture id (pr-NN),
# $3=review file (default review.md). Reads the HIDDEN manifest
# evals/fixtures/review-prs/manifests/<id>.json (never copied into the
# sandbox) and the agent's review.
#
# Rule (PRD FR-9 A/B protocol, no fuzzy adjudication): a defect is DETECTED
# when the review contains a `path:line` (or `path:line-line`) citation whose
# path ends with the defect's file (repo-relative, `head/`-prefixed, or the
# bare basename) and whose line, or line range, falls within ±3 of the
# manifest anchor — `anchor_line`, or any line in `anchors[]` for a defect
# with more than one site.
#
# Parser (1.1.0, bd-ewrc): a leading `(` is not part of the path; comma
# continuations (`path:776,807`, `path:10, 118-121`) and a later bare `:N` or
# `head:N` / `base:N` bind to the most recent cited path. A `:N` glued to a
# word or a number (`note:40`, `10:40`), or with no cited path before it,
# credits nothing.
#
# Parser 1.1.1 (sprint-250 review run 1, n40-n42): the LOA-VERDICT trailer is
# removed before citations are parsed, and a bare `:N` after a quote, bracket,
# brace or `*` (JSON such as `"high":3`) credits nothing; a backtick- or
# bold-wrapped path (`` `b.sh`:40 ``, `**b.sh**:40`) binds its own line; a comma
# continuation or range stays on its line, and a continuation must end at a
# number boundary (no dates);
# a path containing `//` (a URL) is not a citation.
# Run 2 (#11/#13-#15): a match inside any URL token (`scheme://...`) is not a
# citation; a range dash is unspaced and every number (first, continuation,
# bare) ends at a boundary (no further `-N` / `–N`: no dates); the
# quote/bracket guard applies only to the fully bare `:N` (plus a closing
# backtick), so `"head:40"` binds as in 1.1.0; one trailer pattern strips and
# reads the LOA-VERDICT comment and never crosses another comment's bounds.
# Parser 1.1.2 (the run 2 changes above, plus sprint-250 review run 3): the
# URL look-back takes the text after the last whitespace — one linear split —
# so a citation that opens a line never inherits the previous line's URL.
# The parser runs as `python3 -I -` (audit dissent run 1, n32): a module planted
# in the invoker's cwd (a forging json.py) is never imported (RG-27).
#
# Grader 1.2.0 (cycle-129 FR-2, SDD D-2.3): adds the refuted-share figure;
# the recall rule and the pass/score contract are unchanged. A FINDING is one
# distinct cited (path, line-range); it is MATCHED when it overlaps (±3) a
# defect site or a manifest `fix_regions[]` entry ({file, start, end}: the
# head-side lines a record fixture's fix commit touched). details gain
# findings_cited, findings_refuted and refuted_share (refuted / cited; null
# when nothing is cited).
#
# Clean fixtures (0 planted defects) measure FALSE POSITIVES: the LOA-VERDICT
# trailer's critical+high counts; without a trailer, every file:line citation
# counts as one.
#
# Output: {"pass", "score", "details":{recall, planted, detected[], missed[],
#          false_positives, severity_counts, model, effort, tokens}, "grader_version"}
#   pass  = every planted defect detected (defect fixture) / zero false
#           positives (clean fixture); score = recall*100 or 100/0.
# Exit: 0 pass, 1 fail, 2 error (missing manifest / bad args)
#
# Tested by evals/tests/eval-recall-grader.bats.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail

workspace="${1:-}"
fixture="${2:-}"
review_name="${3:-review.md}"

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
MANIFEST_DIR="${EVAL_MANIFEST_DIR:-$SCRIPT_DIR/../fixtures/review-prs/manifests}"

err() { printf '{"pass":false,"score":0,"details":{"error":%s},"grader_version":"1.2.0"}\n' "$(jq -Rn --arg m "$1" '$m')"; exit 2; }

[[ -n "$workspace" && -d "$workspace" ]] || err "invalid workspace"
[[ -n "$fixture" && "$fixture" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || err "invalid fixture id"
manifest="$MANIFEST_DIR/$fixture.json"
[[ -f "$manifest" ]] || err "manifest not found: $manifest"
case "$review_name" in */*|..*) err "review file must be a bare name" ;; esac

review="$workspace/$review_name"
executor="$workspace/.eval/executor.json"

if [[ ! -f "$review" ]]; then
  printf '{"pass":false,"score":0,"details":{"error":"review file not found: %s","planted":%s,"detected":[],"recall":0},"grader_version":"1.2.0"}\n' \
    "$review_name" "$(jq '.defects | length' "$manifest")"
  exit 1
fi

python3 -I - "$manifest" "$review" "$executor" <<'PY'
import json, re, sys
manifest_path, review_path, executor_path = sys.argv[1:4]
man = json.load(open(manifest_path))
text = open(review_path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()

# path:line[-line] citations. Path = something with a file extension; the
# optional trailing range keeps `file.py:10-14` in one token, and the comma
# list after it (`:776,807`) belongs to the same path. A bare `:N` (or
# `head:N` / `base:N`) not glued to a word binds to the most recent path.
# a range dash is unspaced (`a.sh:12 - 40 rows` is prose, not a range) and
# every number ends at a boundary: no letter or digit, and no hyphen / en dash
# before another digit, after it (dates such as 2026-10-05 / 2026–10–05 never
# parse; an open `:369-...` still cites 369) — sprint-250 review run 2, #13
RNG = r'(\d{1,6})(?:[-–](\d{1,6}))?(?![A-Za-z0-9]|[-–]\d)'
CITE = re.compile(
    r'(?P<path>[A-Za-z0-9_./+()-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9]{1,6})[`*)]{0,3}:(?P<first>' + RNG
    + r'(?:[ \t]*,[ \t]*' + RNG + r')*)'
    # head:N / base:N keep the 1.1.0 boundary set ("head:40" binds); the JSON
    # punctuation set, plus a CLOSING backtick (one after a token character:
    # `rows`:40, `"high"`:3), guards only the fully bare :N — an opening
    # backtick (`:7`, (`:212`)) still binds (RG-13) — run 2, #14
    r'|(?:(?<![A-Za-z0-9_./:])(?:head|base)|(?<![A-Za-z0-9_./:"\'{}\[\]*])(?<![A-Za-z0-9_"\'}\]]`)):(?P<bare>' + RNG + r')')
ONE = re.compile(RNG)
cites = []
last = None
# the trailer is machine output (its counts are read below), never a citation.
# One pattern strips and reads it (tolerant whitespace, line breaks); the body
# may not contain another comment's `<!--` or `-->`, so an unterminated
# `<!-- LOA-VERDICT` strips nothing — sprint-250 review run 2, #15
TRAILER = re.compile(r'<!--\s*LOA-VERDICT\s*(\{(?:(?!<!--|-->).)*\})\s*-->', re.S)
body = TRAILER.sub('', text)
URL = re.compile(r'[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]*://|^//')
for m in CITE.finditer(body):
    if m.group("path") is not None:
        # a URL (https://h/x.js:8080, //host.com:8080) is not a path, nor is a
        # partial match that starts later inside the URL token
        # (https://u@h.com/x.js:8080 matches `h.com/x.js`) — run 2, #11
        # the token so far is the window's text after its last whitespace —
        # one linear split ("" when the window ends in whitespace); `\S*$`
        # also matched before a final newline, so a line-leading citation
        # inherited the previous line's URL, and was O(k^2) — run 3
        tok = re.split(r'\s', body[max(0, m.start() - 4096):m.start()])[-1] + m.group("path")
        if "//" in m.group("path") or URL.search(tok):
            continue
        p = m.group("path").lstrip("(")
        if p.startswith("./"):
            p = p[2:]
        last, spans = p, m.group("first")
    elif last is not None:
        p, spans = last, m.group("bare")
    else:
        continue

+def unquote_c(q):
+    """a git C-quoted path body (between the quotes) → text"""
+    i, b = 0, bytearray()
+    while i < len(q):
+        ch = q[i]
+        if ch == "\\" and i + 1 < len(q):
+            n = q[i + 1]
+            if n in "01234567" and re.match(r"[0-7]{3}", q[i + 1:i + 4]):
+                b.append(int(q[i + 1:i + 4], 8))
+                i += 4
+                continue
+            b.extend({"n": b"\n", "t": b"\t", '"': b'"', "\\": b"\\"}.get(n, n.encode()))
+            i += 2
+            continue
+        b.extend(ch.encode())
+        i += 1
+    return b.decode("utf-8", "replace")

+def answer_paths(pr):
+    names = set()

+    for line in text.split("\n"):
+        if line.startswith("diff --git "):
+            rest = line[len("diff --git "):]
+            m = re.fullmatch(Q.replace("((", "a/((", 1) + " " + Q.replace("((", "b/((", 1), rest) or None
+            if m:

+            m = re.fullmatch(r"a/(\S+) b/(\S+)", rest)

+                continue

+            if rest[:2] == "a/" and rest[half + 1:half + 3] == "b/" and rest[2:half] == rest[half + 3:]:
+                names.add(rest[2:half])
+        elif line.startswith(("--- ", "+++ ")):
+            body = line[4:].split("\t", 1)[0]

+        elif line.startswith(("rename from ", "rename to ", "copy from ", "copy to ")):

+def seg_words(seg):
+    try:
+        w = shlex.split(seg, comments=False, posix=True)
+    except ValueError:
+        w = seg.split()
+    while w and (w[0] in SEG_KEYWORDS):
+        w = w[1:]
+    while w and re.match(r"^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=", w[0]) and len(w) > 1:
+        w = w[1:]
+    while w and w[0] in ("command", "env", "builtin", "exec", "nice"):
+        w = w[1:]
+    if w and w[0] == "timeout":
+        w = w[1:]
+        while w and (w[0].startswith("-") or re.match(r"^\d+[smhd]?$", w[0])):
+            w = w[1:]

+def expand(tok, vars_):
+    """$NAME / ${NAME} expansion → list of strings (a loop variable expands to every word); an unknown
+    variable leaves the token unresolved (dropped)"""
+    outs = [tok]
+    for _ in range(4):
+        nxt, changed = [], False
+        for o in outs:
+            m = re.search(r"\$\{([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\}|\$([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)", o)
+            if not m:
+                nxt.append(o)
+                continue
+            name = m.group(1) or m.group(2)
+            if name not in vars_:
+                continue
+            changed = True
+            for v in vars_[name]:
+                nxt.append(o[:m.start()] + v + o[m.end():])
+        outs = nxt
+        if not changed:
+            break
+    return [o for o in outs if "$" not in o]

+def classify(tok, cwd, ws):
+    """→ ("pr", side, rel) | ("ws", rel) | None"""
+    tok = tok.strip("'\"")
+    if not tok or tok.startswith("-") or "://" in tok:
+        return None
+    if tok.startswith("~") or "*" in tok or "?" in tok:
+        return None
+    full = os.path.normpath(tok if tok.startswith("/") else os.path.join(cwd, tok))
+    if full != ws and not full.startswith(ws.rstrip("/") + "/"):
+        return None
+    rel = "" if full == ws else full[len(ws.rstrip("/")) + 1:]
+    if rel == "pr" or rel.startswith("pr/"):
+        rest = rel[3:]
+        for side in ("head", "base"):
+            if rest == side or rest.startswith(side + "/"):
+                return ("pr", side, rest[len(side) + 1:])
+        return ("pr", None, rest)
+    return ("ws", rel)

+def segment_tokens(seg, vars_, cwd, ws):

+    out = []

+def ranges_of(text, sides=("left", "right")):
+    """the printed line ranges of a unified or normal diff on the given sides (left = first operand)"""
+    rs = []
+    for m in HUNK_U.finditer(text):
+        a, n = int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2) or 1)
+        c, k = int(m.group(3)), int(m.group(4) or 1)
+        if "left" in sides:
+            rs.append((a, a + max(n, 1) - 1))
+        if "right" in sides:
+            rs.append((c, c + max(k, 1) - 1))
+    for m in HUNK_N.finditer(text):
+        a = int(m.group(1))
+        c = int(m.group(4))
+        if "left" in sides:
+            rs.append((a, int(m.group(2) or a)))
+        if "right" in sides:
+            rs.append((c, int(m.group(5) or c)))
+    return rs

+def sections(text, targets):
+    """{target: [section body]}: the result split at header lines — a diff header (diff, ---, +++, ***) or
+    a line that is not diff body and names a file (an `echo "=== $f"` marker); a header naming a target
+    (the longest one it holds) opens that target's section, any other header a dropped one; text before
+    the first header belongs to the sole target. Text no header attributes (several targets) is returned
+    as the loose list. Header lines are not part of a body. → (sections, loose)"""
+    out = {f: [] for f in targets}
+    loose = []
+    cur = targets[0] if len(targets) == 1 else None
+    buf = []
+
+    def flush():
+        if buf:
+            (out[cur] if cur is not None else loose).append("\n".join(buf))
+
+    for line in text.split("\n"):
+        diff_hdr = line.startswith(("diff ", "--- ", "*** ", "+++ "))
+        if diff_hdr or (not DIFF_BODY.match(line) and FILEISH.search(line)):
+            named = sorted((f for f in targets if f in line), key=len, reverse=True)
+            hit = named[0] if named else None
+            if line.startswith("+++ ") and hit == cur:
+                continue
+            if hit is not None or diff_hdr or len(targets) > 1:
+                flush()
+                buf = []
+                cur = hit
+                continue
+        buf.append(line)
+    flush()
+    return out, loose

+def fixture_file(root, path):
+    """(bytes, exec) of a regular file at root/path with no symlink component, else None"""
+    cur = root
+    if os.path.islink(cur) or not os.path.isdir(cur):
+        return None
+    parts = path.split("/")
+    for c in parts:
+        cur = os.path.join(cur, c)
+        if os.path.islink(cur):
+            return None
+    try:
+        st = os.lstat(cur)
+    except OSError:
+        return None
+    if not stat.S_ISREG(st.st_mode):
+        return None
+    return open(cur, "rb").read(), bool(st.st_mode & 0o111)

+def tree_blob(repo, commit, path):
+    """(bytes, exec, blob_id) of a regular-file entry in commit, else None"""
+    out = git(repo, "ls-tree", "-z", commit, "--", path)
+    if not out:
+        return None
+    ent = out.split(b"\0")[0].decode("utf-8", "surrogateescape")
+    m = re.match(r"^(\d+) (\w+) ([0-9a-f]+)\t(.*)$", ent, re.S)
+    if not m or m.group(2) != "blob" or m.group(4) != path or m.group(1) not in ("100644", "100755"):
+        return None
+    data = git(repo, "cat-file", "blob", m.group(3))
+    if data is None:
+        return None
+    return data, m.group(1) == "100755", m.group(3)

+def fixture_file(root, path):
+    """(bytes, exec) of a regular file at root/path with no symlink component, else None"""
+    cur = root
+    if os.path.islink(cur) or not os.path.isdir(cur):
+        return None
+    parts = path.split("/")
+    for c in parts:
+        cur = os.path.join(cur, c)
+        if os.path.islink(cur):
+            return None
+    try:
+        st = os.lstat(cur)
+    except OSError:
+        return None
+    if not stat.S_ISREG(st.st_mode):
+        return None
+    return open(cur, "rb").read(), bool(st.st_mode & 0o111)
+
+def tree_blob(repo, commit, path):
+    """(bytes, exec, blob_id) of a regular-file entry in commit, else None"""

+    if not out:
+        return None
+    ent = out.split(b"\0")[0].decode("utf-8", "surrogateescape")
+    m = re.match(r"^(\d+) (\w+) ([0-9a-f]+)\t(.*)$", ent, re.S)
+    if not m or m.group(2) != "blob" or m.group(4) != path or m.group(1) not in ("100644", "100755"):
+        return None
+    data = git(repo, "cat-file", "blob", m.group(3))
+    if data is None:
+        return None
+    return data, m.group(1) == "100755", m.group(3)

513:sgit() {  # git on the sandbox repo, isolated from the operator's git config
538:sgit init -q
539:sgit config user.name eval
540:sgit config user.email eval@loa
541:sgit config commit.gpgsign false
545:sgit add -A
546:sgit commit -q --allow-empty -m base
547:BASE_COMMIT="$(sgit rev-parse HEAD)"
927:    sgit add -A >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
928:    sgit commit -q --allow-empty -m "snapshot $label" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
929:    snap="$(sgit rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)"
931:      sgit bundle create "$SNAPS/$label.bundle" HEAD >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  smoke_root: grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/smoke

trials: {build: 3, review-catch: 3}      # D-A4: review-catch trials 3, not 5, under the gate pipeline
cut_ladder: ["A5, A6, A7 not run", "A2 and A3 build trials 3 -> 2", "A3 review-catch trials 3 -> 2"]   # DEC-0397; A0, A1, A4 keep 3
# Per-run caps (DEC-0559, DEC-0567): from Sprint 261 the cap is per task kind,
# run_usd_by_type {build: 15, review-catch: 20}; run-ablation.sh passes the kind's cap to

local env_gate="" env_copied=false env_sha="" env_src env_dst
  case "$name" in REVIEW) env_gate=review ;; AUDIT) env_gate=audit ;; esac
  if [[ -n "$env_gate" ]]; then
    env_src="$WS/grimoires/loa/a2a/$SPRINT/adversarial-$env_gate.json" env_dst="$EVALD/adversarial-$env_gate.json"
    [[ -e "$env_dst" || -L "$env_dst" || -L "$env_src" || ! -f "$env_src" ]] \
      || { cp "$env_src" "$env_dst" 2>/dev/null && env_copied=true; } || true
    if [[ -f "$env_dst" && ! -L "$env_dst" ]]; then env_sha="$(file_sha256 "$env_dst" 2>/dev/null || true)"; fi
  fi
  if [[ $rc -eq 124 ]] || { [[ $rc -eq 137 ]] && [[ $elapsed_ms -ge $(( tsec * 1000 )) ]]; }; then timed_out=true; fi

  local snap="" verdict=null skill effort_req
  if [[ "$INTERRUPTED" -eq 0 ]] && { [[ "$name" == IMPLEMENT ]] || [[ "$name" == FIX ]]; }; then
    sgit add -A >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    sgit commit -q --allow-empty -m "snapshot $label" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    snap="$(sgit rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [[ -n "$snap" ]]; then
      sgit bundle create "$SNAPS/$label.bundle" HEAD >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
      SNAPSHOTS_JSON="$(jq -c --arg k "$(printf '%s' "$label" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')" --arg v "$snap" '.[$k] = $v' <<<"$SNAPSHOTS_JSON")"
      jq -n --argjson s "$SNAPSHOTS_JSON" --arg base "$BASE_COMMIT" '$s + {base: $base}' > "$SNAPS/index.json"
    fi
  fi
  case "$name" in
    REVIEW) verdict="$(gate_verdict "$WS/grimoires/loa/a2a/$SPRINT/engineer-feedback.md")" ;;
    AUDIT)  verdict="$(gate_verdict "$WS/grimoires/loa/a2a/$SPRINT/auditor-sprint-feedback.md")" ;;
  esac
  if [[ "$name" == REVIEW || "$name" == AUDIT ]]; then LAST_VERDICT="$verdict"; fi

#
# Options:
#   --type <review|audit>     Dissent type (required)
#   --sprint-id <id>          Sprint identifier (required)
#   --diff-file <path>        Path to git diff file (required)
#   --diff-range <base>...<head>
#                             Instead of --diff-file: the script runs `git diff` on the range itself (ref names only)
#   --context-file <path>     Reviewer findings (review only; omit for audit independence)
#   --model <model>           Dissenter model (default: from config or gpt-5.3-codex)
#   --budget <cents>          Max cost in cents (default: from config or 150)
#                             cycle-131 FR-4: flatline_protocol.<code_review|security_audit>.budget_scale: fixed | diff
#                             (default fixed — an absent key is the shipped gate, envelope unchanged) and budget_cents_max
#                             (default 600). diff: the gate's budget is min(max(<this budget>, ceil(estimate × 1.2)),
#                             budget_cents_max), estimate = the pre-dispatch estimate over the planned voices; above it
#                             the run refuses (exit 4, status budget_exceeded, reason budget). A malformed scale or maximum
#                             is said and fixed applies. With the key written the envelope's metadata carries
#                             budget_scale, budget_cents_effective, budget_cents_max.
#
# Findings (cycle-131 FR-4): each finding may carry anchor_line / anchor_line_end (the head-file line, or range, it
# sits on) beside the symbol anchor; kept only as whole numbers 1..10,000,000 (end ≥ start), else dropped silently.

But ablation-row.sh 1.4 itself writes `grader_rule: null` on every ungraded row (interrupted, infrastructure_error, transport_error). So one ungraded row in a batch graded 1.3.0 splits the suite version into "rule pm3" and "rule pm3_or_same_function" partitions, and the ungraded rows leave the primary partition. Reproduced: in the c131 fixture, marking one a3 row `interrupted` with `grader_rule` null moves the primary to "3 · rule pm3_or_same_function" and drops that row from the main exclusions. Interrupted is an exclusion status, so the excluded share and the DEC-0393 degradation guard (inconclusive above 0.25) are undercounted and can be evaded. Only rows that carry a catch figure should take a rule (or a null rule should never split).
head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:135 — when EVAL_HEAD_DIR is unset and `<manifest dir>/../<fixture>/head` is absent, the head tree for the same-scope clause and the citation-validity rule comes from `$workspace/pr/head`. That copy is agent-writable: the sandbox pr/ is copied to grading/pr in ablation-grade.sh, which reaches this fallback whenever `resolve_pr_fixture` raises. An agent can rewrite pr/head/<file> to wrap the file in one definition, which credits any citation in the file through clause (ii). It can also delete the file to switch off the validity rule. Recall must never be computed from agent-controlled input: refuse clause (ii) instead of falling back to the workspace.
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1995 — the KF-046 class 7 exemption accepts any unit that is a substring of a fixture line, whatever the tool. So a Bash command continued onto a new line (`gh repo clone \` then a line holding only `0xHoneyJar/loa`) has a unit that is a substring of the fixture's `github.repository == '0xHoneyJar/loa'` line and is exempt. Likewise, if any fixture file carries `https://github.com/0xHoneyJar/loa`, a WebFetch of that URL is exempt. The upstream-repository probe the repo_name pattern exists to catch is then waved through. Require the unit to be a whole fixture line (or more than the bare token), and do not exempt network-fetch fields.
head/evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml:81 — oracle_closed is added only to a1_full's took_effect. a3_one_voice and a7_effort_medium (line 89) also run review-catch tasks under the closed mount (pipeline-run.sh overlays every mounted review-catch arm), but their runs never get the post-run (a)-(d) check. A mount mutated or opened in those arms goes undetected, while their catch rates are contrasted against a1_full's checked runs. Add oracle_closed to every arm that runs review-catch tasks with the mount.
head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:295 — the one-line-function test (`CLOSE_ONE` = `\{.*\}\s*(?:#.*)?$`) matches a multi-line header whose trailing comment contains a brace expression, e.g. `baz() {  # sets ${X}`. The definition then ends on its header and none of its body has scope. Reproduced: for `baz() {  # sets ${X}` at line 16 with a defect at line 23, a citation of line 17 is not credited. The test should ignore comments, or require the closing `}` to follow a `;`.
head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:271 — markdown headers are matched on every line, including inside fenced code blocks. A ```bash block's `# comment` lines become level-1 headings that cut the enclosing section, so same-section credits are lost in any doc with shell examples. Skip lines inside ``` / ~~~ fences.
head/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:393 — dissent_absent_reason ("disabled" vs "error"/"none") is derived from `sandbox/.loa.config.yaml`, which the agent can rewrite during the run. The grader treats sandbox copies as tamperable and reads the harness copies under eval/ instead. The row should take the planned state from arm evidence or the harness copy of the config, not the sandbox.
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:2010 — corpus_sha256 checks the file with read_regular (no-follow, size cap), discards that text, then re-opens the same path with a plain `open()` (follows symlinks) and hashes that. The digest is not guaranteed to be of the file that was checked. Hash the bytes that read_regular returned (read in binary mode).
head/.loa.config.yaml.example:1643 — the example now writes `budget_scale: fixed` / `budget_cents_max: 600` in both blocks (also line 1707). Every config copied from it therefore has the key "written" (CONF_BUDGET_SCALE_SET=true), and its envelopes gain budget_scale / budget_cents_effective / budget_cents_max plus `reason: budget` on budget_exceeded. That contradicts "an absent key is the shipped gate, envelope unchanged". Either leave the keys commented out in the example or document that copying them changes the envelope.
head/.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh:28 — the new "Findings (cycle-131 FR-4)" paragraph is inserted in the middle of the Options list. `--timeout`, `--dry-run`, `--json` and `--record-fallback` now read as part of the Findings note. Move it after the options.
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

content.text:
The review is in `/workspace/review.md`: 10 findings and the verdict **CHANGES_REQUIRED**. Nothing under `pr/` was changed.

**Blocking findings**
- **The report drops ungraded rows from the main analysis** (`ablation-report.py:1135`). The row writer stores no grader rule on rows that were never graded (for example interrupted runs), and the report reads that as a separate rule. One such row splits the suite version into two groups, and the main analysis uses only the larger one. Interrupted rows are part of the excluded share, so the 0.25 degradation guard undercounts and can be dodged. I reproduced this with the PR's own report fixture: marking one row interrupted produced two partitions.
- **The grader can read the agent's own copy of the PR** (`recall-vs-defects.sh:135`). When no fixed head directory is available, it uses `pr/head` inside the agent's workspace, which the agent can edit. Rewriting those files lets the new same-function rule credit almost any citation, and deleting them switches off the citation-validity check.
- **The repo-name contamination exemption can be bypassed** (`ablation-grade.sh:1995`). Text counts as quoting the PR if it appears anywhere inside a fixture line. Putting the bare repo name on its own continuation line of a Bash command passes that test. So does a WebFetch of the repo's GitHub URL, if any fixture file contains it.
- **Only one arm gets the post-run mount check** (`ablation-2.0.yaml:81`). Only `a1_full` has `oracle_closed`. `a3_one_voice` and `a7_effort_medium` run review tasks under the same closed mount but are never checked after the run.

**Lower-severity findings**
- **Grader misreads some function headers** (`recall-vs-defects.sh:295`). A header with a comment such as `# sets ${X}` is treated as a one-line function, so citations in its body are not credited. I reproduced this with a small test file.
- **Markdown code comments become headings** (`recall-vs-defects.sh:271`). `#` comment lines inside code blocks are read as headings and cut sections short.
- **Dissent-absence reason comes from a file the agent can edit** (`ablation-row.sh:393`). It reads the sandbox config rather than a harness-owned copy.
- **Corpus digest may hash a different file than it checked** (`ablation-grade.sh:2010`). It checks the file safely, then reopens it in a way that follows symlinks and hashes that.
- **The example config sets the new budget keys** (`.loa.config.yaml.example:1643`). Any config copied from it changes the review output, which contradicts the "absent key, output unchanged" promise.
- **Help text is out of place** (`adversarial-review.sh:28`). A new paragraph is inserted in the middle of the options list.

I did not review the test files beyond the report test fixtures I used for the reproduction.
